api_analysis.hypothesis: The compile error arises because the identifier 'tanh' in the binding file is ambiguous: it refers to the global CUDA math function tanh (from <cmath> or cuda_runtime.h) and also to the wrapper function torch::Tensor tanh(torch::Tensor x). Passing &tanh to pybind11::module_::def resolves to an overload set that pybind cannot deduce, causing 'no matching function for call'.
evidence: Error: no matching function for call to 'pybind11::module_::def(const char [5], <unresolved overloaded function type>, const char [13], pybind11::arg)' at custom_ops_binding.cpp:106, where m.def("tanh", &tanh, ...) is called.
The binding file includes <cuda_runtime.h> and <torch/types.h>, which may bring the global C tanh function into scope, creating an overload set with the wrapper function.
Even without the C tanh, the wrapper function name 'tanh' may conflict with std::tanh if 'using namespace std' or similar is present.
The contract-driven binding fragments expect the function names and arguments exactly, but the ambiguity is a C++ compile-time issue.
changes: Rename the C++ wrapper functions to avoid conflict with the standard math function. For clarity, rename 'tanh' to 'tanh_forward' and 'maxpool1d' to 'maxpool1d_forward'. Update the corresponding m.def entries to use the new names, keeping the pybind export names 'tanh' and 'maxpool1d' as required by the contract.

Ensure no global 'tanh' is brought into scope; avoid using namespace std and avoid including unnecessary headers that might introduce it. The current includes are probably fine with renamed functions.

After renaming, the pybind registration will be: m.def("tanh", &tanh_forward, "Tanh forward", py::arg("x")); and m.def("maxpool1d", &maxpool1d_forward, "MaxPool1d forward", py::arg("x"), py::arg("kernel_size"), py::arg("stride"), py::arg("padding"));
This change is minimal and directly addresses the overload resolution failure.
